explanations.answer: To the entrance to the Tent of Meeting
explanations.explanation: Yes, friend. The sisters approach the entrance to the Tent of Meeting and stand before Moses, Eleazar the priest, the leaders, and the whole congregation (Numbers 27:2). Then they speak up and make their case. Five sisters, one entrance, and a whole congregation to hear it. I respect that a whole lot.

explanations.answer: To the banks of the Jordan
explanations.explanation: The Jordan is a river, and it's a good guess, but the sisters never go there in this passage. They approach the entrance to the Tent of Meeting and stand before Moses, Eleazar the priest, the leaders, and the whole congregation (Numbers 27:2). If you tried to make your case by a river, friend, you'd mostly be talking to the water.

Manasseh is the ancestor of their clans, so I see why you picked it. The sisters belong to the clans of Manasseh son of Joseph (Numbers 27:1). But the text sends them to the entrance to the Tent of Meeting, where they stand before Moses, Eleazar the priest, the leaders, and the whole congregation (Numbers 27:2). That's a big audience for five sisters.

Not quite, friend. The sisters say the opposite: their father "…was not among the followers of Korah who gathered together against the LORD." (Numbers 27:3). Korah led a rebellion (Numbers 16:1-3), and the sisters say their dad was not part of it. Then they add that he died because of his own sin, and they say that plainly too.

That's right, friend. The sisters say their father "…was not among the followers of Korah who gathered together against the LORD." (Numbers 27:3). Korah's rebellion was a big, loud mess (Numbers 16:1-3), and they made sure their dad's name stayed out of it. Then they said he died because of his own sin, and they didn't dodge that either.

Exactly. They say, "Give us property among our father’s brothers." (Numbers 27:4). Their dad had no sons, and they didn't want his name to disappear from his clan. Five sisters, one clear request, no rambling. I've seen grown folks take twenty minutes to ask for a napkin.

explanations.answer: A seat among their clan's leaders
explanations.explanation: A seat sounds fancy, but that's not what they ask for. They say, "Give us property among our father’s brothers." (Numbers 27:4). Their request is about property and their father's name, not a title. I think they came with a plan, and the plan had a very short list.

Nope, no matchmaking in this passage. The sisters ask, "Give us property among our father’s brothers." (Numbers 27:4). Husbands never come up in their request. They walked in with one item on the list, and it was property.

explanations.answer: He brings it before the LORD
explanations.explanation: Yes, friend. "…Moses brought their case before the LORD…" (Numbers 27:5). Five sisters had just made their request, and Moses took it to the LORD. I think that's the right move when a question is that big. The LORD answers him in the very next verse (Numbers 27:6).

explanations.answer: He hands it to the leaders
explanations.explanation: The leaders are standing right there, so I get it. But the text says Moses "…brought their case before the LORD…" (Numbers 27:5). He doesn't pass it down the line. Moses takes it to the One who actually has the answer.

Eleazar, the priest, is standing there too, so that's a fair guess. But the text never mentions lots here. It says Moses "…brought their case before the LORD…" (Numbers 27:5). No coin flip needed when you can ask the LORD Himself.

That's right. The LORD says, "The daughters of Zelophehad speak correctly." (Numbers 27:7). Five sisters stood up in front of everybody, and the LORD agreed with them. I think that's the kind of sentence you'd frame and hang over the oven.

Careful, friend, this one flips the verse. The LORD tells Moses, "The daughters of Zelophehad speak correctly." (Numbers 27:7). They had come to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting and asked for property among their father's brothers (Numbers 27:2-4). Moses brought their case to the LORD, and that's the answer that came back. I'd say the sisters got a stamp of approval, and I know a little something about waiting for one of those.

Yes, friend. The LORD says to give them property "…and transfer their father’s inheritance to them." (Numbers 27:7). That's what the sisters came asking for. Their father's inheritance goes to his daughters, right there among their father's brothers.

Debts, ha! Nobody wants those in the cookie box. But they're not in this verse. The LORD says to transfer their father's inheritance to them (Numbers 27:7). That's something given to the sisters, not a bill.

Duties sounds official, but that's not what the verse says. The LORD tells Moses, "You certainly must give them property as an inheritance among their father’s brothers and transfer their father’s inheritance to them." (Numbers 27:7). The property is their inheritance, and it's given to them. Nobody handed these five a to-do list.

That's it, friend. "If a man dies and leaves no son, you are to transfer his inheritance to his daughter." (Numbers 27:8). The sisters had asked for property among their father's brothers, and here the LORD tells Moses to say this to the Israelites. It becomes a rule for the whole nation, not just one family. I think those five sisters standing at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting got an answer bigger than their question.

I see why you'd think of her, but the LORD names someone else. "If a man dies and leaves no son, you are to transfer his inheritance to his daughter." (Numbers 27:8). The widow isn't named in this rule. It's the daughter who comes next after sons.

The clan's leader doesn't show up in this rule at all. The LORD says, "If a man dies and leaves no son, you are to transfer his inheritance to his daughter." (Numbers 27:8). The inheritance stays with the man's own household first. That's good news for five sisters in particular.

Right on, baker. "If he has no daughter, give his inheritance to his brothers." (Numbers 27:9). The LORD's rule goes in order: son first, then daughter, then brothers. And the order keeps going, because the next verse covers what happens if there are no brothers (Numbers 27:10).

Servants aren't in the list, friend. The LORD says, "If he has no daughter, give his inheritance to his brothers." (Numbers 27:9). The inheritance stays in the family line. It doesn't wander off to the household help.

Nice neighbors are a blessing, but they're not in this rule. The LORD says, "If he has no daughter, give his inheritance to his brothers." (Numbers 27:9). The line keeps going through the man's own family first. Nobody's getting a surprise inheritance because they lived next door.
Not quite, friend. The LORD says to give it "…to the next of kin from his clan…" (Numbers 27:11). It stays in the clan, not with another tribe. That's the last step in the whole line.

Correct. When there are no children, no brothers, and no brothers of the father, the LORD says, "…give his inheritance to the next of kin from his clan…" (Numbers 27:11). It stays in the clan, not with another tribe. That's the last step in the list the LORD gives.
